name: Jerez

climate: Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

keyfacts: Palomino makes about 90 percent of sherry grapes, and Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel are used for sweet wines.
The best vineyards are on albariza, an almost white soil that keeps moisture through the hot summer and suits Palomino best.
Fino and Manzanilla age under a layer of flor, while oloroso develops no flor and oxidizes as it ages.
Amontillado is first aged under flor and then exposed to oxygen, which makes it darker than a fino but lighter than an oloroso.
In the solera system, wine moves through several tiers of barrels, so most sherry carries no vintage, and VOS and VORS mean at least 20 and 30 years average age.

blurb.text: The DO for sherry, made from white grapes grown around Jerez de la Frontera in Andalusia. Palomino makes styles from light fino to darker, oxidized amontillado and oloroso. Manzanilla, from Sanlúcar de Barrameda, has its own DO. Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel make sweet dessert sherries.
